name: MySQL
description: MySQL 5.7 and later, MariaDB 10.3 and later (detected from the version banner), and compatible services (Aurora MySQL, Cloud SQL, Azure Database for MySQL, PlanetScale). A MySQL database is what other systems call a schema, so the hierarchy has one level, database. Reads information_schema; one connection serves every database.

properties.label: Database
properties.help: Database to read. Empty and no list below: every database you can see.

properties.label: Databases to read
properties.help: *: every database you can see. Or a list; wildcards allowed.

properties.help: Needed for caching_sha2_password logins without TLS.

version.sql: select version() as version, concat(@@version_comment, ' ', version()) as banner

test.sql: select current_user() as login, database() as current_database, version() as version

source.sql: select 'MySQL' as product, version() as version, concat(@@version_comment, ' ', version()) as banner, current_user() as login

sql: select s.schema_name as name, s.default_character_set_name as charset,
case t.table_type when 'BASE TABLE' then 'table' when 'VIEW' then 'view' when 'SYSTEM VIEW' then 'view'
nullif(t.table_comment, '') as comment, t.table_rows as row_count,
t.data_length + t.index_length as size_bytes, t.create_time as created_at, t.update_time as updated_at,
t.engine as engine, v.view_definition as definition
left join information_schema.views v on v.table_schema = t.table_schema and v.table_name = t.table_name
[[and cast(t.table_name as binary) > cast({{after}} as binary)]]
select c.table_name as dataset, c.ordinal_position as ordinal, c.column_name as name, c.column_type as data_type,
c.is_nullable as nullable, c.column_default as default_value, nullif(c.column_comment, '') as comment,
c.extra like '%auto_increment%' or c.generation_expression <> '' as is_generated,
c.character_maximum_length as max_length, c.numeric_precision as numeric_precision,
select k.table_name as dataset, k.constraint_name as name,
lower(replace(tc.constraint_type, ' ', '_')) as type, k.column_name as columns,
k.referenced_table_schema as ref_database, k.referenced_table_name as ref_dataset,
k.referenced_column_name as ref_columns, k.ordinal_position as seq
on k.constraint_schema = tc.constraint_schema and k.constraint_name = tc.constraint_name
select s.table_name as dataset, s.index_name as name, s.non_unique = 0 as is_unique,
s.index_name = 'PRIMARY' as is_primary, lower(s.index_type) as method, s.column_name as columns,
select r.routine_name as name, lower(r.routine_type) as type, 'SQL' as language,
r.dtd_identifier as returns, nullif(r.routine_comment, '') as comment, r.definer as owner
select u.view_name as dataset, u.table_schema as upstream_database, u.table_name as upstream_dataset,
select p.table_name as dataset, p.grantee as principal, p.privilege_type as privilege,
select concat(u.user, '@', u.host) as name, 'user' as type, u.account_locked = 'N' as can_login,
select c.table_name as dataset, c.ordinal_position as ordinal, c.column_name as name, c.column_type as data_type,
c.is_nullable as nullable, c.column_default as default_value, nullif(c.column_comment, '') as comment,
c.extra like '%auto_increment%' as is_generated, c.character_maximum_length as max_length,
c.numeric_precision as numeric_precision, c.numeric_scale as numeric_scale

overlays.description: MariaDB has no view_table_usage and keeps users in mysql.global_priv; account_locked is not in mysql.user.

sql: select concat(u.user, '@', u.host) as name, case when u.is_role = 'Y' then 'role' else 'user' end as type,
